Keep a small watchlist. Expand it when a question calls for a new perspective.
The useful outcome is knowing what to try, update or reconsider.

## Follow people who show their work

```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://simonwillison.net/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Simon Willison&#x27;s Weblog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Hands-on model experiments, annotated releases, practical tools, and prompt-injection coverage.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://hamel.dev/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hamel Husain&#x27;s Blog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Concrete guidance on looking at data, debugging failures, and measuring AI products.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://latent.space/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Latent Space</a><small>newsletter</small></div><p>An AI engineering publication with builder interviews, analysis, and news discovery.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://eugeneyan.com/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Eugene Yan</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Practical essays and prototypes about reliable AI products, search, and evaluation.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://huyenchip.com/blog/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Chip Huyen&#x27;s Blog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Useful frameworks for system design, production applications, and model tradeoffs.</p></li></ul>
```

## Know when the ground changes

```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">API changelog</a><small>official changelog</small></div><p>Dated changes that can invalidate older recipes.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">API deprecations</a><small>official lifecycle reference</small></div><p>Authoritative shutdown timelines prevent adopting retired interfaces.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://huggingface.co/blog" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Blog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Practical releases and explanations from Hugging Face and its wider community.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://www.anthropic.com/engineering" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Anthropic Engineering</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Detailed accounts of building, evaluating, and deploying agent systems.</p></li></ul>
```

## Find ideas before they become tutorials

```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Daily Papers</a><small>research</small></div><p>A community-curated front door to new research and linked implementations.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://openreview.net/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">OpenReview</a><small>research</small></div><p>Conference papers with reviews, author responses, and acceptance context where venues make them public.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hacker News</a><small>forum</small></div><p>A useful place to discover tools, failure stories, and skeptical engineering discussion.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/show" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Show HN</a><small>forum</small></div><p>A stream of tools and prototypes posted by their builders.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@aiDotEngineer" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">AI Engineer — YouTube</a><small>youtube</small></div><p>Conference talks and workshops from practitioners building AI systems.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://www.interconnects.ai/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Interconnects — Nathan Lambert</a><small>newsletter</small></div><p>Research-informed commentary on model development, post-training, and the open-model ecosystem.</p></li></ul>
```

## Give an update somewhere to land

For a development worth keeping, record four things:

- **What changed?** Link to the original announcement, paper or repository.
- **Why does it matter here?** Connect it to a question or something you are building.
- **What is the evidence?** Separate the source’s claim from a result you have reproduced.
- **What would you try?** Choose one bounded experiment, or record why no action is needed.

::: {.connection-note}
This is a curated watchlist. New releases and event dates need a fresh check; it is not an automated news feed.
:::
